rationale: Escalate the active consequence candidate to an obligation and run it. The confirmed durability defect leaves a node with a latest configuration whose index holds no configuration entry; the follower heartbeat path then admits a campaign under that adopted voter set, and the leader commit path marks configurations.latest committed whenever its index falls within the commit index, without consulting the entry stored there. The check drives that whole path with two connected in-memory nodes and observes whether the committed configuration is backed by a configuration entry.

candidate.rationale: A configuration that reaches the committed state without a supporting log entry would let a node compute quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease from a voter set no log agrees with, so the responsibility is fixed for the selected scenario and executed directly.

question.question: Can a node that adopted a configuration whose log entry was never durably stored later commit that configuration as its committed configuration, for example after regaining leadership with the vote of a fresh peer?
question.importance: A committed configuration that no log entry supports would make this node and its peers disagree about the voter set that defines quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease; a node could then treat a server as a voter (or a previous voter as removed) without any agreed log entry, which is a consensus-safety consequence of the confirmed configuration-durability defect rather than only a local inconsistency.
contexts: a node whose configuration entry write failed and which therefore holds a latest configuration not present in its log
a fresh peer that joins with an empty configuration and log
event_paths: AddVoter fails its StoreLogs, dispatchLogs answers the error and sets state Follower, and appendConfigurationEntry still publishes the new latest configuration
the follower heartbeat timer observes latestIndex different from committedIndex and the local server being a voter of the latest configuration, then transitions to Candidate
electSelf requests votes for the next term from the latest configuration's voters and the fresh peer grants one
the leader commits an entry of its term and the commit path marks configurations.latest as committed because latestIndex is now within the commit index

supporting_behavior_ids.b-config-change: establishes the latest configuration from the leader-side change path whose durable write failed
supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-quorum: consumes the voter set of the latest configuration when deciding what can be committed

counterevidence: the node alone cannot command a majority of the phantom voter set, so adopting the configuration does not by itself commit it
processConfigurationLogEntry is the only intended writer of configuration state from an actual log entry
unknowns: Whether a fresh peer with an empty configuration actually grants the vote to the node holding the phantom configuration
Whether the node can satisfy the commitment gate for an entry of its own term in that configuration and thereby mark the phantom configuration committed
question.trigger_rationale: The confirmed check stopped at the post-failure state. The next discriminating step is whether the adopted configuration can reach the committed state: the follower heartbeat path admits a campaign whenever latestIndex differs from committedIndex and the local server is a voter of the latest configuration, so a node in that state may campaign under the phantom voter set; a fresh peer with an empty configuration has no membership veto and no log to compare against, so whether it grants the vote, and whether the leader can then satisfy the commitment gate for its own term, decides the proposition.

obligation.description: A server must not treat a configuration as committed unless the log entry at that configuration index is a configuration entry encoding that configuration, so the voter set used for quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease is always backed by an agreed log entry.

scope.description: One node that adopted an unpersisted configuration and later returned to the leader state with the vote of a fresh peer, compared with the log entry at its committed configuration index.
assumptions: the node's configuration entry write failed once, so its latest configuration has no supporting entry
the joining peer starts without a configuration, as a fresh node does
excluded: recovery routes where a surviving majority repairs the log
whether such a committed configuration survives a restart

pending: Whether the committed phantom configuration survives a restart and is re-derived from the log is retained as an open question.

grounding.derivation: configurations.committed is the latest configuration in the log or snapshot that has been committed, and configurations.latestIndex is the index where that configuration was written; appendConfigurationEntry can advance latestIndex without a stored entry, and the leader commit path promotes configurations.latest to committed whenever latestIndex lies within the new commit index without checking the entry kind at that index. The responsibility therefore separates what the node believes is committed from what the log actually encodes.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the selected two-node scenario in which the node holds an adopted configuration whose entry was never stored and then regains leadership; the ordinary path with a stored configuration entry is unaffected.
unresolved: Restart behaviour of a committed configuration with no supporting entry
alternatives: checking the entry kind at the configuration index before promoting it is one design alternative; the obligation fixes the responsibility, not that repair

associations.rationale: This declaration contains the leader commit path that promotes the latest configuration to committed once its index falls within the commit index, without inspecting the entry stored at that index.

bindings.description: Raft.leaderLoop: the leader commit path that marks the latest configuration committed.
